sections.heading: What is Type complexity budgets and team conventions?

blocks.text: **Type complexity budgets and team conventions** is a compile-time TypeScript concept that erases at emit — the run-time behavior is still JavaScript. Type complexity budgets and team conventions is where JavaScript dynamic typing surprises C# developers — implicit ToNumber, ToString, and truthiness rules that === and Object. sections.heading: Why Type complexity budgets and team conventions matters in production

blocks.text: Senior interviews and on-call debugging both test **Type complexity budgets and team conventions** beyond one-line definitions. Production failures here look like silent data corruption, memory growth, type errors at CI, or async ordering bugs — not syntax errors. If you know JavaScript, use the comparison table to transfer intuition instead of memorizing rules in isolation.

Pitfalls for Type complexity budgets and team conventions
blocks.body: Treating Type complexity budgets and team conventions as pure syntax without compile-time or run-time behavior. Skipping validation at API/JSON boundaries. Ignoring strict compiler flags differences. Hand-waving in design review without a test or metric.

blocks.text: Prove mastery of **Type complexity budgets and team conventions** with a failing test that captures the edge case, a DevTools or heap snapshot showing the bug, and a clear tradeoff statement in design review. Senior interviewers want mechanism — what the compiler and emitted JS actually do — plus when the simple explicit version beats the clever abstraction.
